_comment: Real-world project audit manifest. Phase 66 confidence-followup §1a. Each entry: a real-world project pinned to a specific commit, its install directory (sometimes a subpath inside a monorepo), and a smoke command that exercises a meaningful slice of the project. The harness clones --depth 1 at the pinned ref, replaces the project's install with `lpm install --linker hoisted` and `--linker isolated` separately, and reports asymmetric outcomes the same way as bench/audit-fixtures. Add new entries here; the suite runner picks them up automatically.

projects.name: next-blog-starter
projects.why: Next.js + React + remark/rehype markdown pipeline. Exercises the React peer-dep instance invariant + Webpack plugin discovery via Next's compiler.

projects.name: astro-basics
projects.why: Astro + Vite + multiple integrations. Exercises Astro's plugin ecosystem and Vite peer requirements simultaneously.
projects.smoke: npx --no-install astro check && npx --no-install astro build

projects.name: vite-vue-ts
projects.why: Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript starter shape. Exercises Vue's reactive-system peer chain plus volar/vue-tsc through Vite's plugin layer.

projects.name: nest-typescript-starter
projects.why: NestJS deep DI + decorator peer chain (rxjs + reflect-metadata + class-validator). Real-world version of audit-fixtures/peer-heavy/nestjs-deep with a full TS build.

projects.name: remix-blues-stack
projects.why: Remix + Prisma + Vitest + Playwright. Exercises bundler integration with React peers + Prisma codegen postinstall.
projects.smoke: npx --no-install prisma generate && node -e "require('@remix-run/node'); require('@prisma/client'); console.log('require chain ok')"

projects.name: vite-react-ts
projects.why: Minimal Vite + React + TS. Lighter than Next.js but exercises the same React-peer + Vite-plugin invariants. Used as a smoke-control: if this fails the whole audit is suspect.

projects.name: vitepress-install
projects.why: Vue + Markdown-it + Shiki. Exercises the heavy plugin chain on install: ~250 transitives across the Vue ecosystem, vite-plugin-vue, Algolia search, Shiki syntax highlighting. Smoke is `import('vitepress')` — proves install correctness + ESM resolution from the v2 store layout. Full doc-site builds rely on project config files which would couple this audit to vitepress's own quirks; the install graph itself is the unit-under-test.
projects.smoke: node --input-type=module -e "const m = await import('vitepress'); if (typeof m.defineConfig !== 'function') { throw new Error('vitepress.defineConfig not exported'); } console.log('vitepress import ok');"

projects.name: eleventy-base-blog
projects.why: 11ty + a heavy plugin chain (rss, syntaxhighlight, navigation). Tests SSG plugin discovery and `.bin` link materialization. The smoke is narrowed to `--version` because the project's full build uses Nunjucks `{% include 'node_modules/prismjs/themes/...' %}` — a literal filesystem-path include of a transitive dependency. npm/yarn hoist all transitives to project-root `node_modules/`; lpm (both isolated AND hoisted) keeps transitives inside per-package wrapper dirs in the v2 store. **Both lpm linker modes fail this build symmetrically — this is an lpm-vs-npm compatibility decision, NOT a hoisted-default confidence gap.** Tracked separately; the asymmetric-only gate doesn't catch it because both modes diverge from npm equally.

projects.name: express-mongoose-api
projects.why: Express + Mongoose. Backend stack with a deep transitive native-module chain (bson, mongoose internals).

projects.name: hardhat-tutorial
projects.why: Hardhat + ethers + native solc bindings. Combines compile-on-install + heavy native deps + plugin chain.
